01
Before the first verse · Vol. 4, p. 644

Opening of the surah

Vol. 4, p. 644
Sūrat al-Muddaththir is Meccan, and it has fifty-six verses [revealed after al-Muzzammil]. In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.
سورة المدثر مكية، وهي ست وخمسون آية [نزلت بعد المزمل] بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ
02
Q 74:1–5 · Vol. 4, pp. 644–646

Verses 1 to 5

The verses as the commentary quotes them
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. “O you who are wrapped in a cloak (1), arise and warn (2), and your Lord, magnify (3), and your garments, purify (4), and uncleanliness, avoid (5)
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم يا أَيُّهَا الْمُدَّثِّرُ (1) قُمْ فَأَنْذِرْ (2) وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ (3) وَثِيابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ (4) وَالرُّجْزَ فَاهْجُرْ (5)
Vol. 4, p. 644
.” Al-muddaththir is the one who wears the dithār, which is what is worn over the shiʿār, the garment that touches the body. From this comes the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: “The Anṣār are the shiʿār and the people are the dithār.” [2] It was said that this is the first sūra to be revealed. Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh transmitted from the Messenger of God ﷺ: “I was on Mount Ḥirāʾ when a voice called: ‘O Muḥammad, you are the Messenger of God.’ I looked to my right and my left and saw nothing, then I looked above me and saw something.” [3] And in
الْمُدَّثِّرُ لابس الدثار، وهو ما فوق الشعار: وهو الثوب الذي يلي الجسد. ومنه قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام «الأنصار شعار والناس دثار» «2» وقيل: هي أوّل سورة نزلت. وروى جابر بن عبد الله عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «كنت على جبل حراء فنوديت: يا محمد، إنك رسول الله، فنظرت عن يمينى ويساري فلم أر شيأ، فنظرت فوقى فرأيت شيأ» «3» . وفي
Vol. 4, p. 645
the report of ʿĀʾisha: “I looked above me, and there he was, seated on a throne between heaven and earth, meaning the angel who had called him. I was terrified and returned to Khadīja and said: ‘Cover me, cover me.’ Then Gabriel came down and said: ‘O you who are wrapped in a cloak.’” From al-Zuhrī: the first thing revealed was Sūrat Iqraʾ bi-smi rabbika up to the words “what he did not know.” The Messenger of God ﷺ grew sad and began to climb the tops of high mountains. Gabriel came to him and said: “You are the Prophet of God.” He returned to Khadīja and said: “Cover me and pour cold water over me.” Then “O you who are wrapped in a cloak” was revealed. [2] It was also said that he heard something he disliked from Quraysh and was distressed, so he covered himself with his garment, deep in thought, as a distressed person does. He was then commanded not to abandon warning them, even if they made him hear what he disliked and harmed him. From ʿIkrima: he read it in the passive participle form, from dathkharahu (daththarahu), and said: “This matter has been wrapped around you and bound to you,” as He said in al-Muzzammil: “Arise from your bed.” Or the sense is: arise with resolve and determination. “And warn”: caution your people about God's punishment if they do not believe. The sound view is that the meaning is: perform the warning, without restricting it to any one person. “And your Lord, magnify”: single out your Lord for takbīr, which is to describe Him with greatness and to say “God is greatest.” It is related that when this was revealed the Messenger of God ﷺ said “God is greatest,” and Khadīja said takbīr, rejoiced, and was certain that it was revelation. It may also be taken to refer to the takbīr of the prayer. The fāʾ enters with the sense of a condition, as if it said: whatever happens, do not abandon magnifying Him. “And your garments, purify”: a command that his garments be free of impurities, because the purity of garments is a condition of the prayer, which is not valid without it, and it is better and more beloved outside the prayer as well; it is ugly for a good believer to carry filth. It was also said that it is a command to shorten them, and to differ from the Arabs in lengthening their garments and trailing their hems, which does not guarantee against contact with impurities. It was also said that it is a command to purify the self from despicable deeds and from habits regarded as shameful. One says “so-and-so is pure in his garments,” “pure in his pocket, hem, and sleeves” when describing him as free of defects and stains of character, and “so-and-so is filthy in his garments” of the treacherous. The reason is that the garment accompanies a person and wraps around him, so it is used as a metonym for him. Do you not see their saying “Zayd, his garment pleased me,” as they say “Zayd, his mind and character pleased me,” and they say “glory is in his garment” and “generosity is beneath his cloak.” It is also because the common case is that one who has purified and cleaned his inner self takes care to purify and clean the outer, and refuses to do anything but avoid filth and prefer purity in everything. “And uncleanliness” (al-rujz) is read with kasra and with ḍamma; it means punishment, and the meaning is: avoid what leads to it, the worship of idols and other sins. The meaning is to persist in avoiding it, because he was already free of it.
رواية عائشة: «فنظرت فوقى فإذا به قاعد على عرش بين السماء والأرض- يعنى الملك الذي ناداه- فرعبت ورجعت إلى خديجة فقلت: دثروني دثروني، فنزل جبريل وقال: «يا أيها المدثر» » وعن الزهري: أوّل ما نزل: سورة اقرأ باسم ربك إلى قوله ما لَمْ يَعْلَمْ فحزن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وجعل يعلو شواهق الجبال، فأتاه جبريل فقال: إنك نبىّ الله، فرجع إلى خديجة وقال: دثروني وصبوا علىّ ماء باردا، فنزل: يا أيها المدثر «2» . وقيل: سمع من قريش ما كرهه فاغتم، فتغطي بثوبه مفكرا كما يفعل المغموم. فأمر أن لا يدع إنذارهم وإن أسمعوه وآذوه. وعن عكرمة أنه قرأ على لفظ اسم المفعول. من دثره. وقال: دثرت هذا الأمر وعصب بك، كما قال في المزمّل: قم من مضجعك. أو قم قيام عزم وتصميم فَأَنْذِرْ فحذر قومك من عذاب الله إن لم يؤمنوا. والصحيح أنّ المعنى: فافعل الإنذار من غير تخصيص له بأحد وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ واختص ربك بالتكبير: وهو الوصف بالكبرياء، وأن يقال: الله أكبر. ويروى أنه لما نزل قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الله أكبر» فكبرت خديجة وفرحت، وأيقنت أنه الوحى، وقد يحمل على تكبير الصلاة، ودخلت الفاء لمعنى الشرط. كأنه قيل: وما كان فلا تدع تكبيره وَثِيابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ أمر بأن تكون ثيابه طاهرة من النجاسات، لأنّ طهارة الثياب شرط في الصلاة لا تصح إلا بها، وهي الأولى والأحب في غير الصلاة، وقبيح بالمؤمن الطيب أن يحمل خبثا. وقيل: هو أمر بتقصيرها، ومخالفة العرب في تطويلهم الثياب وجرهم الذيول، وذلك ما لا يؤمن معه إصابة النجاسات. وقيل: هو أمر بتطهير النفس مما يستقذر من الأفعال ويستهجن من العادات. يقال: فلان طاهر الثياب وطاهر الجيب والذيل والأردان إذا وصفوه بالنقاء من المعايب ومدانس الأخلاق. وفلان دنس الثياب للغادر، وذلك لأنّ الثوب يلابس الإنسان ويشتمل عليه، فكنى به عنه. ألا ترى إلى قولهم: أعجبنى زيد ثوبه، كما يقولون: أعجبنى زيد عقله وخلقه، ويقولون: المجد في ثوبه، والكرم تحت حلته، ولأنّ الغالب أنّ من طهر باطنه ونقاه عنى بتطهير الظاهر وتنقيته، وأبى إلا اجتناب الخبث وإيثار الطهر في كل شيء وَالرُّجْزَ قرئ بالكسر والضم، وهو العذاب، ومعناه: اهجر ما يؤدى إليه من عبادة الأوثان وغيرها من المآثم. والمعنى: الثبات على هجره، لأنه كان بريئا منه.
Vol. 4, p. 646

03
Q 74:6–7 · Vol. 4, p. 646

Verses 6 to 7

The verses as the commentary quotes them
“And do not confer favor to acquire more (6), and for your Lord be patient (7)
وَلا تَمْنُنْ تَسْتَكْثِرُ (6) وَلِرَبِّكَ فَاصْبِرْ (7)
Vol. 4, p. 646
.” Al-Ḥasan read walā tamnun, and tastakthiru is in the nominative, but in the accusative position as a ḥāl, that is: do not give while regarding what you give as much, or while seeking much. It is a prohibition of istighzār, which is to give something while hoping to be compensated by the recipient with more than was given. This is permissible, and from it comes the ḥadīth: “The one who seeks increase is rewarded for his gift.” [1] There are two explanations of it. One is that it is a prohibition specific to the Messenger of God ﷺ because God Almighty chose for him the noblest manners and the finest character. The other is that it is a prohibition of refinement, not of prohibition, for him and his community. Al-Ḥasan also read tastakthir with sukūn. This has three explanations. The first is that it is a substitute for tamnun, as if it said: “do not give, do not seek more,” taking it from al-mann in His words “then they do not follow what they spent with reminders of favor or injury,” because it is the way of one who reminds others of his gifts to regard them as much, that is, to see them as great and count them. The second is that it is likened to ʿaḍud (thus making a sukūn in lightening), and the third is that it takes the state of pausing into account. Al-Aʿmash read it in the accusative with an implied “an,” as in the verse: “Ah, you who forbid me to attend the fray…” [2] This is supported by the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: walā tamnun an tastakthira. In the nominative reading it is possible to drop “an” and cancel its effect, as it is reported that “aḥḍuru al-wagha” is also read in the nominative. “And for your Lord be patient,” that is, for the sake of God, so apply patience. It was said: patience with the harm of the polytheists. It was said: patience in performing the obligations. From al-Nakhaʿī: patience in your giving, as if he connected it with what precedes it and made it patience in giving without regarding it as much. The better view is that it is a command to the act itself, and that it extends generally to everything that is borne patiently and everything one is patient against, with patience under the harm of the unbelievers intended, because it is one of the things the general term includes.
قرأ الحسن: ولا تمنّ. وتستكثر، مرفوع منصوب المحل على الحال، أى: ولا تعط مستكثرا رائيا لما تعطيه كثيرا، أو طالبا للكثير: نهى عن الاستغزار: وهو أن يهب شيئا وهو يطمع أن يتعوّض من الموهوب له أكثر من الموهوب، وهذا جائز. ومنه الحديث «المستغزر يثاب من هبته» «1» وفيه وجهان، أحدهما: أن يكون نهيا خاصا برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لأنّ الله تعالى اختار له أشرف الآداب وأحسن الأخلاق. والثاني: أن يكون نهى تنزيه لا تحريم له ولأمّته. وقرأ الحسن: تستكثر، بالسكون. وفيه ثلاثة أوجه، الإبدال من تمنن. كأنه قيل: ولا تمنن لا تستكثر، على أنه من المنّ في قوله عز وجل ثُمَّ لا يُتْبِعُونَ ما أَنْفَقُوا مَنًّا وَلا أَذىً لأنّ من شأن المنان بما يعطى أن يستكثره، أى: يراه كثيرا ويعتدّ به، وأن يشبه ثرو بعضد، فيسكن تخفيفا، وأن يعتبر حال الوقف. وقرأ الأعمش بالنصب بإضمار «أن» كقوله: ألا أيّهذا الزّاجرى أحضر الوغى «2» وتؤيده قراءة ابن مسعود: ولا تمنن أن تستكثر. ويجوز في الرفع أن تحذف «أن» ويبطل عملها، كما روى: أحضر الوغى بالرفع، وَلِرَبِّكَ فَاصْبِرْ ولوجه الله، فاستعمل الصبر. وقيل: على أذى المشركين. وقيل: على أداء الفرائض. وعن النخعي: على عطيتك، كأنه وصله بما قبله، وجعله صبرا على العطاء من غير استكثار. والوجه أن يكون أمرا بنفس الفعل، وأن يتناول على العموم كل مصبور عليه ومصبور عنه، ويراد الصبر على أذى الكفار، لأنه أحد ما يتناوله العام.

Q 74:8–10 · Vol. 4, pp. 646–647

Verses 8 to 10

The verses as the commentary quotes them
“For when the trumpet is blown (8), that, on that day, will be a difficult day (9), for the unbelievers not easy (10)
فَإِذا نُقِرَ فِي النَّاقُورِ (8) فَذلِكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ (9) عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ (10)
Vol. 4, p. 646
.” The fāʾ in “for when the trumpet is blown” is causal, as if He said: be patient with their harm, for before them lies a difficult day on which they will meet the consequence of their harm, and on which you will meet the consequence of your patience under it. The fāʾ in “that” is for the apodosis.
والغاء في قوله فَإِذا نُقِرَ للتسبيب، كأنه قال: اصبر على أذاهم، فبين أيديهم يوم عسير يلقون فيه عاقبة أذاهم، وتلقى فيه عاقبة صبرك عليه. والفاء في فَذلِكَ للجزاء.
Question
If you ask: what governs the accusative of idhā, and how can “on that day” be an adverb of “a difficult day”?
فإن قلت: بم انتصب إذا، وكيف صح أن يقع يَوْمَئِذٍ ظرفا ليوم عسير؟
Answer
I answer: idhā is governed by what the apodosis indicates,
قلت: انتصب إذا بما دلّ
Vol. 4, p. 647
because the meaning is: when the trumpet is blown, the matter will be hard for the unbelievers. What permitted “on that day” to be an adverb of “a difficult day” is that the meaning is: that, at the time of the blowing, is the occurrence of a difficult day, because the Day of Resurrection comes and occurs when the trumpet is blown. There is disagreement whether this is the first blast or the second. It is also possible that “on that day” is indeclinable, in the nominative position, as a substitute for “that,” with “a difficult day” as the predicate, as if it said: “the day of the blowing is a difficult day.”
عليه الجزاء، لأنّ المعنى: فإذا نقر في الناقور عسر الأمر على الكافرين، والذي أجاز وقوع يَوْمَئِذٍ ظرفا ليوم عسير: أنّ المعنى: فذلك وقت النقر وقوع يوم عسير، لأنّ يوم القيامة يأتى ويقع حين ينقر في الناقور. واختلف في أنها النفخة الأولى أم الثانية. ويجوز أن يكون يومئذ مبنيا مرفوع المحل، بدلا من فَذلِكَ ويَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ خبر، كأنه قيل: فيوم النقر يوم عسير.
Question
If you ask: what is the point of the words “not easy,” when “difficult” already makes it unnecessary?
فإن قلت: فما فائدة قوله غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ وعَسِيرٌ مغن عنه؟
Answer
I answer: when He said “for the unbelievers,” restricting the difficulty to them, He said “not easy” to signal that for them it will not be easy and light as it will be for the believers, so that it combines a threat to the unbelievers, an increase of their rage, and good news and consolation for the believers. It is also possible that the meaning is that it is difficult, with no hope that it will become easy, unlike the hope that a difficult matter of this world will be eased.
قلت: لما قال عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ فقصر العسر عليهم قال: غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ ليؤذن بأنه لا يكون عليهم كما يكون على المؤمنين يسيرا هينا، ليجمع بين وعيد الكافرين وزيادة غيظهم وبشارة المؤمنين وتسليتهم. ويجوز أن يراد أنه عسير لا يرجى أن يرجع يسيرا، كما يرجى تيسر العسير من أمور الدنيا.
